problem: The ARM7TDMI name is unpacked as 'ARM7 core, Thumb, debug support and a multiplier'. The letters are T, D, M, I — the I (EmbeddedICE) is dropped and D and I are merged into one vague phrase.
fix: T = Thumb, D = debug support (JTAG), M = enhanced 64-bit multiplier, I = EmbeddedICE macrocell for in-circuit debug.

problem: 'C means carry or borrow' is loose. In ARM the C flag is the carry out of the ALU; after a subtraction C = 1 means no borrow, so a student may read C = 1 as 'a borrow happened'.
fix: C is the carry out of the ALU. For subtraction it is the inverted borrow: C = 1 means no borrow, C = 0 means a borrow was needed.

problem: 'An operating system uses it to run privileged code without a mode switch' is misleading — entering System mode is itself a mode switch. The point being made is that no register bank changes.
fix: System mode is privileged but uses the User register bank, so privileged code can run with the User registers and stack without switching to another bank.

problem: The wording is inverted and confusing: R13, R14 and R15 are exactly the hardware names; it is SP, LR and PC that are software conventions. A student can read this as saying R13–R15 are not defined by the architecture.
fix: R13, R14 and R15 are plain registers with no hardwired function. SP, LR and PC are the roles software assigns to them by convention; the core only acts on R13, R14 and R15.
